questions.q: A circular economy is a change away from which model?
options: Renting instead of owning
Producing goods only locally
Resources are mined, made into products and then become waste
Recycling everything that is produced
questions.explain: A circular economy keeps materials in use; material recovery plays an important role.
questions.evidence: It is a change to the model in which resources are mined, made into products, and then become waste.

questions.q: What are the major stages in a material's life cycle?
options: Raw material acquisition, materials manufacture, production, use/reuse/maintenance and waste management
Buying, selling and storing
Mining and landfilling only
Design, marketing and sales
questions.explain: Sustainable materials management looks at impacts across the whole life cycle.
questions.evidence: The major stages in a material’s lifecycle are raw material acquisition, materials manufacture, production, use/reuse/maintenance, and waste management.

questions.q: What does EPA mean by municipal solid waste (MSW), or trash?
options: Only hazardous industrial waste
Waste water from homes
Mining waste
Various items consumers throw away after they are used
questions.explain: Examples include bottles, boxes, food, grass clippings, furniture and appliances.
questions.evidence: EPA refers to trash, or MSW, as various items consumers throw away after they are used.

questions.q: In the EU waste hierarchy, what is the preferred option, and what is the last resort?
options: Recycling is preferred; prevention is the last resort
Preventing waste is preferred; landfill is the last resort
Incineration is preferred; recycling is the last resort
Landfill is preferred; composting is the last resort
questions.explain: Order: prevention, preparing for re-use, recycling, other recovery, disposal.
questions.evidence: Preventing waste is the preferred option, and sending waste to landfill should be the last resort.

options: Burning waste to make energy
Burying waste safely
Collecting and processing materials that would otherwise be thrown away and turning them into new products
Selling used goods second-hand
questions.explain: Collection, processing and manufacturing into new products repeat as a loop.
questions.evidence: Recycling is the process of collecting and processing materials that would otherwise be thrown away as trash and turning them into new products.

questions.q: How does applying compost to land help the climate?
options: Carbon is stored in the soil instead of being released into the atmosphere
It cools the air above fields
It reflects sunlight back into space
It removes methane from landfill
questions.explain: Compost also builds soil health and supplies nutrients to plants.
questions.evidence: When we apply compost to the land, carbon is stored in the soil instead of being released into the atmosphere.

questions.q: Why do waste producers play a key role under the waste duty of care?
options: They own the landfill sites
They set the price of disposal
They issue waste licences
They are in the best position to identify the nature and characteristics of the waste
questions.explain: An accurate description travels with the waste so it can be handled safely.
questions.evidence: Waste producers play a key role under the duty of care requirements as they are in the best position to identify the nature and characteristics of the waste.

questions.q: What is a householder's waste duty of care limited to?
options: Recycling every item
Taking all reasonable measures to ensure their waste is only transferred to an authorised person
Paying a waste tax
Keeping waste at home for a year
questions.explain: Using an unlicensed 'man with a van' can make householders liable.
questions.evidence: limited to taking all reasonable measures available to them to ensure their waste is only transferred to an authorised person.

questions.q: Before transferring waste to another person, what must a waste holder ensure?
options: That the person pays for it
That the waste is recycled abroad
That the person has the correct authorisation
That the waste is mixed with other waste
questions.explain: Transfers must go to registered carriers or permitted sites.
questions.evidence: Ensure that any person you transfer the waste to has the correct authorisation

questions.q: How is waste from a property used mainly for commercial business classed?
options: As commercial waste, subject to the duty of care
As household waste
As hazardous waste in every case
It is not regulated
questions.explain: Businesses run from homes still follow the commercial duty of care for that waste.
questions.evidence: Waste that comes from a property or part of a property that is mainly used for commercial business is regarded as commercial waste
